model_note.S:
cc: Lightheadedness after standing

HPI: 29 yo m. Patient reports: It began 3 days ago. It feels like lightheadedness in my head, not spinning. There is no pain radiating anywhere. My vision dims and I feel faint. It lasts about 20 seconds and I need to hold a chair. It happens after standing, then settles. My blood pressure medicine dose increased last week. Sitting or lying down makes it stop. Standing quickly and hot showers provoke it. I started standing more slowly. I have not had this before. My vision dims when I stand.

Patient perspective: I am scared I will fall while I am alone.

PMH: Hypertension; no heart disease or diabetes.

PSH: No operations or prior hospital admissions.

Meds: Hydrochlorothiazide increased from 12.5 mg to 25 mg daily last week.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Never smoked tobacco. One glass of wine weekly. No recreational drugs. Librarian; lives with wife; has been drinking less water to avoid bathroom trips.

FH: My mother is sixty-two and she has high blood pressure.; My father died of pneumonia when he was eighty.; I have one brother, he's thirty-two and he's healthy.

ROS: Neurologic - Reports presyncope. Denies vertigo. Denies focal weakness. Cardiovascular - Denies syncope. Denies palpitations. Denies chest pain. Gastrointestinal - Denies melena. Denies vomiting. Denies diarrhea.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 98.3 F oral, P 78 bpm, BP 126/76 mmHg seated, R 16 rpm, Pulse Ox 99% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert. Comfortable while seated.

Heart: Regular rhythm, S1 and S2 without murmur. After 5 minutes supine BP 126/76, pulse 78; at 1 minute standing BP 102/64, pulse 92 with lightheadedness; at 3 minutes standing BP 104/66, pulse 90.

Lungs: Breath sounds clear bilaterally.

Neuro: Strength 5/5 in both arms and legs.

Osteopathic: T1 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.

Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Measure orthostatic vitals safely and obtain ECG, BMP and CBC; review the recent dose change with the prescribing clinician before altering therapy; discuss hydration if not contraindicated, slow standing and fall precautions; follow up within 48 hours and seek emergency care for syncope, chest pain or focal deficits.

2. Obtain ECG and consider ambulatory monitoring if unexplained or recurrent; assess exertional episodes and family sudden death; arrange cardiology review if rhythm or risk findings warrant it. Educate the patient to sit or lie down promptly if symptoms recur and to avoid situations in which another episode could cause injury while the cause is being assessed.

3. Check CBC and ask about blood loss; investigate any identified anemia rather than empirically treating without a cause; explain emergency precautions for bleeding or worsening weakness. Arrange follow-up to review the CBC and any bleeding history within 48 hours if stable enough for outpatient care; active bleeding or worsening presyncope requires immediate reassessment.

model_note.S:
cc: Lightheadedness after standing

HPI: 29 yo m. Patient reports: It began 1 day ago. It feels like lightheadedness in my head, not spinning. There is no pain radiating anywhere. My vision dims and I feel faint. It lasts about 20 seconds and I need to hold a chair. It happens after standing, then settles. My blood pressure medicine dose increased last week. Sitting or lying down makes it stop. Standing quickly and hot showers provoke it. I started standing more slowly. I have not had this before. My vision dims when I stand.

Patient perspective: I am scared I will fall while I am alone.

PMH: Hypertension; no heart disease or diabetes.

PSH: No operations or prior hospital admissions.

Meds: Hydrochlorothiazide increased from 12.5 mg to 25 mg daily last week.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Never smoked tobacco. One glass of wine weekly. No recreational drugs. Librarian; lives with wife; has been drinking less water to avoid bathroom trips.

FH: My mother is sixty-two and she has high blood pressure.; My father died of pneumonia when he was eighty.; I have one brother, he's thirty-two and he's healthy.

ROS: Neurologic - Reports presyncope. Denies vertigo. Denies focal weakness. Cardiovascular - Denies syncope. Denies palpitations. Denies chest pain. Gastrointestinal - Denies melena. Denies vomiting. Denies diarrhea.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 98.3 F oral, P 78 bpm, BP 126/76 mmHg seated, R 16 rpm, Pulse Ox 99% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert. Comfortable while seated.

Heart: Regular rhythm, S1 and S2 without murmur. After 5 minutes supine BP 126/76, pulse 78; at 1 minute standing BP 102/64, pulse 92 with lightheadedness; at 3 minutes standing BP 104/66, pulse 90.

Lungs: Breath sounds clear bilaterally.

Neuro: Strength 5/5 in both arms and legs.

Osteopathic: T1 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.

Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Measure orthostatic vitals safely and obtain ECG, BMP and CBC; review the recent dose change with the prescribing clinician before altering therapy; discuss hydration if not contraindicated, slow standing and fall precautions; follow up within 48 hours and seek emergency care for syncope, chest pain or focal deficits.

2. Obtain ECG and consider ambulatory monitoring if unexplained or recurrent; assess exertional episodes and family sudden death; arrange cardiology review if rhythm or risk findings warrant it. Educate the patient to sit or lie down promptly if symptoms recur and to avoid situations in which another episode could cause injury while the cause is being assessed.

3. Check CBC and ask about blood loss; investigate any identified anemia rather than empirically treating without a cause; explain emergency precautions for bleeding or worsening weakness. Arrange follow-up to review the CBC and any bleeding history within 48 hours if stable enough for outpatient care; active bleeding or worsening presyncope requires immediate reassessment.

model_note.S:
cc: Lightheadedness after standing

HPI: 29 yo m. Patient reports: It began 3 days ago. It feels like lightheadedness in my head, not spinning. There is no pain radiating anywhere. My vision dims and I feel faint. It lasts about 20 seconds and I need to hold a chair. It happens after standing, then settles. My blood pressure medicine dose increased last week. Sitting or lying down makes it stop. Standing quickly and hot showers provoke it. I started standing more slowly. I have not had this before. My vision dims when I stand.

Patient perspective: I am scared I will fall while I am alone.

PMH: Hypertension; no heart disease or diabetes.

PSH: No operations or prior hospital admissions.

Meds: Hydrochlorothiazide increased from 12.5 mg to 25 mg daily last week.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Never smoked tobacco. One glass of wine weekly. No recreational drugs. Librarian; lives with wife; has been drinking less water to avoid bathroom trips.

FH: My mother is sixty-two and she has high blood pressure.; My father died of pneumonia when he was eighty.; I have one brother, he's thirty-two and he's healthy.

ROS: Neurologic - Reports presyncope. Denies vertigo. Denies focal weakness. Cardiovascular - Denies syncope. Denies palpitations. Denies chest pain. Gastrointestinal - Denies melena. Denies vomiting. Denies diarrhea.

Patient concern: I have stairs at home and nobody there during the day.

General: Alert. Comfortable while seated.

Heart: Regular rhythm, S1 and S2 without murmur. After 5 minutes supine BP 126/76, pulse 78; at 1 minute standing BP 102/64, pulse 92 with lightheadedness; at 3 minutes standing BP 104/66, pulse 90.

Lungs: Breath sounds clear bilaterally.

P: 1. Measure orthostatic vitals safely and obtain ECG, BMP and CBC; review the recent dose change with the prescribing clinician before altering therapy; discuss hydration if not contraindicated, slow standing and fall precautions; follow up within 48 hours and seek emergency care for syncope, chest pain or focal deficits. Develop a specific fall-prevention and check-in plan with the patient rather than merely advising caution.

2. Obtain ECG and consider ambulatory monitoring if unexplained or recurrent; assess exertional episodes and family sudden death; arrange cardiology review if rhythm or risk findings warrant it. Educate the patient to sit or lie down promptly if symptoms recur and to avoid situations in which another episode could cause injury while the cause is being assessed.

3. Check CBC and ask about blood loss; investigate any identified anemia rather than empirically treating without a cause; explain emergency precautions for bleeding or worsening weakness. Arrange follow-up to review the CBC and any bleeding history within 48 hours if stable enough for outpatient care; active bleeding or worsening presyncope requires immediate reassessment.
